name: Wideband (2.5-14 GHz) cryogenic feed receiver: quad-ridged flared horn, high-pass filter, noise coupler and LNAs cooled to 15 K in a GM cryostat with Mylar RF window; Y-factor receiver temperature with 295 K absorber
plain_name: Cool an entire radio antenna feed horn to 15 K and measure how much noise it adds
description: Arecibo 12 m telescope receiver: the QRFH, 2.5 GHz high-pass filters, noise couplers and Citcryo1-12D LNAs are enclosed in a cryostat built around a two-stage GM cryocooler (Trillium 350CS cold head, M600 compressor) and cooled to 15 K; signals enter through a Mylar window under a dry-air radome; receiver temperature (median 25 K over 2.5-14 GHz) is measured by the Y-factor method with a 295 K absorber as hot load and the sky as cold load.
keywords: Cool an entire radio antenna feed horn to 15 K and measure how much noise it adds

sources.citation: D. A. Roshi, P. Perillat, F. Fernandez, H. Mani et al., 'A Cryogenic Wideband (2.5 - 14 GHz) Receiver system for the Arecibo 12m Telescope', Radio Science (2023), arXiv:2308.05826

requirements.rationale: The horn, filter, coupler and LNA are cooled to 15 K.
Sky and hot-load radiation reach the cold horn through the cryostat RF window (Mylar).
The cold RF chain must carry 2.5-14 GHz.
The cold components are in an evacuated cryostat monitored by a vacuum gauge.
LNA gate/drain bias and monitoring wiring must reach the cold amplifiers.
Optional: the cryostat uses a two-stage GM cryocooler (no liquid cryogen), suited to a telescope-mounted receiver.

confirmation_note: Requirements taken from the cited procedure and independently re-verified against the source (research/v4, 2026-11-01). Users must confirm them for their own run; edits require confirmation again.
